# Appeal of Denial – Rotator Cuff Repair (CPT 29827)

**Molina Clinical Policy MCP-404 Shoulder Arthroscopy**
https://www.molinahealthcare.com/-/media/Molina/PublicWebsite/PDF/Providers/il/resource/Shoulder-Arthroscopy-Guidelines_MCP_404.pdf

**Member:** Cameron Grant
**Member ID:** W314904804
**Plan:** Molina Healthcare (Commercial/ACA), Arizona
**Denial date:** 2026-08-08
**Reference number:** POC-9DD444765E-23652

Dear Molina Healthcare Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), which was denied on 2026-08-08 as not medically necessary. I am requesting reconsideration of this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this surgery is medically necessary, and I believe the records show that I meet the plan's own published criteria.

## Why I believe my records meet the plan's criteria

The policy documentation I have been given, Molina Clinical Policy MCP-404, lists medical-necessity criteria for several shoulder arthroscopy procedures, including diagnostic arthroscopy, debridement, and others. I do not have a copy of a criteria section written specifically for rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), so I am relying on the general criteria language that has been provided to me and that appears across these sections. I am requesting below that Molina confirm and provide the exact criteria section it applied to my case.

The policy states:

> "Severe, disabling pain and/or a documented loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living;"

My records show that I have had 24 months of progressive shoulder pain that has not improved with rest, and that I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side. This is a documented loss of function that interferes with everyday activities.

The policy also states:

> "and  Failure of non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration including at least two of the following as appropriate:"

My records document more than three months of non-surgical treatment: 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (20 visits, 2026-05-20 to 2026-07-15) focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, documented in the physical therapy discharge note; 8 months of NSAID use with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-08 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. This is more than one form of conservative treatment, sustained well beyond three months, without lasting improvement.

The policy also states:

> "and  Demonstration of functionally limited range of motion (active or passive) on physical examination as compared to the non-involved side  Failure of non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration, including at least two of the following as appropriate:"

My exam findings show range of motion limited by pain and positive provocative testing on the affected side.

In addition, my MRI from 2026-06-05 shows a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy, which my surgeon has documented as the basis for his recommendation that surgical repair is medically necessary.

## Request for the specific criteria applied

Molina's own utilization-management materials state that the criteria used for review are MCG-based and available through the secure provider portal, and that members may call Member Services to obtain the criteria used to make a final determination. I am asking that Molina provide, in writing, the MCG guideline title and the specific criteria applied to my determination, including the section that applies to rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) specifically, so that I and my surgeon can review it in full.

## What I am asking for

I ask that Molina reconsider this denial in light of the records described above and the plan's own published criteria, and that Molina approve coverage for my rotator cuff repair. I also ask that Molina send me the specific MCG criteria applied to my case, as described above.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-04. I am submitting this appeal through the address printed on my denial letter, and I understand I can also check my status or submit documents through the Molina member portal at molinahealthcare.com or by calling the Member Services number on my ID card.

Please let me know if any additional information is needed from me or from Dr. Okafor's office.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Cameron Grant
Member ID: W314904804
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

---

*This letter was prepared to help me communicate with my health plan. It is not medical or legal advice, and it does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
